attributes.mbcameraupdate_finding: THE 8-BYTE FRAME SURPLUS IS GONE AND NEITHER DENIAL COULD SAY SO. Both MBCameraUpdate denials rest on `ours stwu r1,-48(r1) against target stwu r1,-40(r1)` / `frame target 40 ours 48` and both test it through `probe.py ... --slots`, which reads the postprocessed object of a pinned function. Measured on the RAW body: `wf_word_diff --list` returns 18 differing words over 159/159 instructions and NOT ONE OF THEM IS A FRAME INSTRUCTION -- the frames agree. The shipped source state is the accumulator form the v2 record itself recorded as PROBE C (`frame 40/40, SLOT MAP IDENTICAL, real 34, multiset IDENTICAL, exactly 2 aligned IMMEDIATE rows'), and the live raw read is that exact shape: `DECODE: REGFIELD-ONLY 16, IMMEDIATE 2`. The two IMMEDIATE words are the induction pair v2's own falsifier names -- `+0x01e4 O 39290010 T 38840004` and `+0x01ec O 38630004 T 38630010`, i.e. addi-by-16 against addi-by-4 -- and they are absorbed by the shipped rule's second `instruction_permutation` window, which is declared over exactly `start 0x1e4, end 0x1f0, order [2,1,0]`. So: v1, whose scope IS the frame surplus, denies a thing that no longer exists and is a stale_solved candidate; v2's exclusivity claim (frame and band are not simultaneously source-reachable) is CONFIRMED by what shipped -- source took the frame, the postprocessor took the band -- but its premise line and its expiry trigger must be restated on the raw read.

attributes.refined_law: THE RUN-51 LAW IS TRUE BUT ITS FAILURE MODE IS ONE OF TWO, AND THE SECOND IS THE MORE DANGEROUS. 'Can never fire' describes a trigger keyed on a reading the postprocessed object gives BY CONSTRUCTION (real 0, an IDENTICAL multiset, no ROLE MISMATCH row): those checks pass forever. But a trigger keyed on a NONZERO premise value -- `real 18`, `real 48`, `real 6`, `frame target 40 ours 48`, `the four cluster lines at @424-@440`, `target-only +1 mr / ours-only -1 li` -- ALWAYS FIRES on a pinned function, because the postprocessed read can never show the value it demands. That is a FALSE EXPIRY: it tells the next lane a live denial has lapsed. Counted over the thirteen: 2 are never-fire (CL_crittergettargetplayers, SB_do-enemies) and 9 are always-fire. Both modes are unfalsifiable in practice and both need the same cure -- read the raw body -- but only the second one destroys standing conclusions, and the run-51 law's title names the harmless half.
